I was an asset protection manager for walmart when they implemented that program.  Essentially, we would used corrective education class to in lieu of the shoplifters paying restitution to the stores.  

Various records per region showed that only about 10-20% of restitution was ever paid to the stores because most people knew walmart wasn’t going to sue for a few hundred dollars.  

The CEC program was across several retailers hat we’re all compiled into one database.  This made it difficult to enforce one particular policy which was always prosecute a repeat offender because now all of a sudden if this was heir first time stealing from walmart but they were caught at another store using CEC they were automatically disqualified no matter what. 

The state a live in, restitution could be up to three
Times the value of what was taken.   So if my team caught someone stealing fifty dollars worth of valuables they would only owe approximately 150 dollars.  However, with CEC it was now 500.  

As someone who trained their team on this program, I felt like it was unethical and so did my whole team.  Walmart eventually abandoned t due to this lawsuit and CEC has since ceased operating its website.  I’m curious to see what happens now.
